correctness.rationale: The proof reduces the sharp coefficient functional to complex Hölder against a two-frequency kernel. Since the sharp constant exceeds one, both target coefficients of an extremizer are nonzero; strict Hölder equality then forces exactly the stated cosine-power boundary trace, and direct integration proves the converse. The full spectrum follows from an exact Fourier recurrence for \(G(u)=|\cos u|^{r+1}\), with the Gamma formula checked against its base coefficient and recurrence. The recurrence terminates exactly for positive odd \(r\). Index rigidity follows because classified continuous boundary traces at order \(n\) have exactly \(2n\) zeros per circle. A standalone finite numerical checker confirms representative coefficients, recurrence, and truncation but is explicitly not used as an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The motivating 2026 source proves the sharp constant and gives an explicit cosine-power witness, but its inspected full text does not state the converse equality characterization or the resulting complete spectrum, discrete finite-spectrum phase, or coefficient-index rigidity. Targeted database searches for the claim, aliases and consequences returned no matching published finding. Older and contemporaneous coefficient papers inspected or cross-checked give bounds, selected equality examples, or a p=infinity extremal classification rather than the finite-p theorem here. A specific residual risk remains because the full Shi-Li-Lian paper was not openly accessible during review.
residual_risks: The complete text of doi:10.1007/s40315-025-00600-8 was not available through accessible open sources during this review, so an equivalent finite-p equality classification hidden outside the accessible theorem statement cannot be ruled out absolutely.

The closed Gamma formula for cosine-power Fourier coefficients is classical and is used only as supporting algebra; originality is asserted for the combined equality classification and structural consequences, not for that identity alone.

value.rationale: The sharp constant was newly identified in the motivating 2026 work, making its equality geometry a natural structural gap. The result answers that gap completely for \(1<p<\infty\), identifies every coefficient of every extremizer, finds an exact discrete set of exponents where extremizers become trigonometric polynomials, and proves that extremizer families for distinct coefficient orders are disjoint. These are intrinsic structural properties of the sharp inequality rather than an arbitrary parameter slice or a recomputation of the constant.
